Appeal from Original Decree No. 601 of 1991
With
Civil Rule No. 261 (FM) of 1991
lawyer:
Mr. Sajjad Ali Chowdhury, A.A.G, ------ For the Appellants
Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate ------ For the Respondent
parties:
Upazila Nirbabi Officer, Bajitpur ------ Appellant
Vs.
Maijchar Matshajibi Samabaya Samity ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Muhammad Ansar Ali, J.: This First Miscellaneous Appeal at the instance of the defendants is directed against the judgment and order dated 15.6.1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Kishorganj, in other class Suit No. 73 of 1990 allowing the plaintiffs application for temporary injunction under Order 29, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 The plaintiff-respondent instituted the above suit in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Kishorganj on 11.8.90 praying for certain. declarations, namely, for declaration of its lease-hold right in the Maijchar Jalmahal (Fishery) within Bajitpur Upazila of the Kishorganj District up to 30th Chaitra, 1397 B.S. and for further declaration that the plaintiff is entitled to compensatory extension of its lease for a further period of 3 years arid that the decision of the Upazila Jalmahal Management / Co-ordination Committee dated 23.7.90 declaring the 'plaintiff Samity as fake one being not allegedly composed of fishermen is illegal and void and not binding upon the plaintiff Samity and further it is entitled to take part in the next auction of the government fishery in question; that the suit proceeded and sometime thereafter the plaintiff Samity: on 13.5.93 filed all application under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendants particularly defendants Nos. 7 and 8 from disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in the said Fishery and also from giving, effect to the decision dated 23.7.90 of the Upazila Fishery Management Co- ordination Committee barring the plaintiff from taking part in the next auction of the said fishery. 

 4. The case of the plaintiff petitioners as narrated in the application for temporary injunction was that the plaintiff Samabaya Samity was formed with 59 fishermen and registered' as such oil 17.1.87 under the Co-registered Societies Act and that the Maijchar Jainahal (hereinafter called the suit-fishery) is a closed fishery within, the Bajitpur Upazila of the Kishorganj district and the Government as a    special case leased out the said fishery to the plaintiff Samity for 3 years with effect from 1395 B.S.i.e. up to 30th Chaitra 1397.B.S. at a yearly rent of Tk. 87,725/-, that for proper management of the fisheries situated within the Bajitpur Upazila, Upazila Fishery Management Co-ordination Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Upazila Management Committee, was formed with defendants No. 1 as the Chairman and defendant No. 2 to 4 as members and defendant No. 5 as the member secretary and the defendant No. 6 Who-earlier-had very strained relationship with the secretary of the plaintiff. Samity only with a view to creating unnecessary obstacles and problems. in. the .enjoyment of the said suit-fishery by the plaintiff held a so called inquiry and declared the plaintiff samity as a fake one and debarred it from taking part in the public auction of the government-fisheries on the alleged ground that it was unfit for participation in any auction further case of the plaintiff samity was that it had invested a huge sum of money for the development of the fishery in question but it could not catch and rear up fishes, though the period of lease was going to be over and hence the plaintiff samity  applied for compensatory extension of its earlier lease of the fishery for a further period of 3 years w.e.f. 1398 B.S. but the said application was not considered by the authority and meanwhile the period of lease being expired, the defendants prepared to lease out the fishery by public auction for the years 1398-1400. B.S and accordingly fixed 15.5.91 as the date for holding auction of the suit-fishery. The plaintiff samity having learnt about the same, tiled the instant application for temporary injunction on 13.5.91 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Subordinate Judge thereupon Asked the defendants to show cause and on receipt of the notice, the local Government Pleader entered appearance in Court on behalf of the defendants Nos. 7 and 8 and took time till 19.5.91 for filing objection. But meanwhile the auction of the, suit fishery as notified rlier was held on 15.5.91 and the same was leased out to the Maijchar Dhoanadi Matsajibi Samabaya Samity being the alleged highest bidder and the new lessee Samity deposited a sum of Tk. 2,75,112/00 with the lesee for the said period i.e., for the years 1398-1400 B.S. This fact was brought to the notice of the Court by the plaintiff and accordingly an order of status quo dated 16.5.91 was obtained. The defendants Nos. 7 and 8 then filed a written objection denying all the material allegations made in the application for temporary injunction and further contending that on a Government decision, an enquiry was held through Upazila Management Committee as to the genuineness of the plaintiff Samity and it was found that the plaintiff Samity was a fake one, of its 56 members only a lbw were fishermen, 28 of them were absentee having no connection with the Samity and the rest were agriculturists. Apart from that chairmen of the 3 local Union Parishads namely, Maijchar Union. Parishad, Baliadi Union Parishad and the Dilalpur Union Parishad also submitted their reports apparently showing that the plaintiff was a fictitious one having no genuine fishermen and then in a meeting of the Upazila Management committee held on 23.7.90, it was unanimously resolved and decided that the plaintiff Samity was not competent to take part in any auction of the government fisheries it being and fictitious one and the said decision of the Management Committee, was communicated to the higher authorities including the Registrar of the Co-operative Societies and thereafter the Registrar was pleased to direct the District, Co-operative Officer to take necessary steps for winding up the plaintiff Samabaya Samity. It was further contended in the written objection that in view of the provisions of Sections 86, 132 and 133 of the Co-operative Societies Act, 1940, the suit of the plaintiff' was not Maintainable' in the Civil court and further the Plaintiff Samity did not deposit the entire lease money of its, lease as per-terms the lease deed and further on the expiry of the period of its lease for 3 year on the 30th Chaitra 1387, B.S; the plaintiff has or had no right to remain in possession of the, suit-fishery and also has or had no right for claiming the case hold-right in the said fishery. It was further contended in the written objection that the plaintiff Samity had no primafacie case and it would not suffer any irreparable loss or injury zit the temporary injunction, was not granted in its favour and that Government have every right to lease, out the fishery to any society of the fishermen in accordance with the rules and its decision and further the plaintiff was not entitled to any temporary injunction as Prayed for against the government department particularly the instant case in connection with the management of the fishery which involves activities of auction as already held on 15.5.91, five, Fishermen co-operative Societies took part and the Maijchar Daonadi Motsliajibi Samabaya Samity being the highest bidder at Tk. 2,75,112/- was declared to be lessee of the suit fishery for the years 1398- 1400 B.S. which samity at once deposited 56% of the bid money with the Govt. 

 5. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge after hearing the learned Advocates of both the parties and on consideration of the materials on record came to a finding that the plaintiff Samity had a primafacie arguable case and as per rule 205(3) of the Government Estate Manual the plaintiff samity was entitled to get lease of the fishery question for a further period of 3 years. By way of extension of its earlier lease and that the decision of the Management Committee declaring the plaintiff Samity as a fake one and debarring it from taking part in any auction of the govt. fisheries was primafacie illegal and upon such observations allowed the application for temporary injunction by his judgment and order dated 15.6.91. against defendants Nos. 7 and 8 on contest and also cancelled the now auction held on 15.5.91. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge, the defendants have preferred this Misc. Appeal in this Court. After the admission of the said appeal under Order 41 Rule 11 C.P.C. the defendant-appellant filed an application praying for stay of the operation of the impugned order dated 15.6.91 upon which a Rule was issued by a Division Bench of this court on 21.8.91 and also an ad-interim order of stay was granted for 3 months and thereafter it was extended from time to time and lastly on 1.8.592 again for 3 months. Meanwhile the First Misc. Appeal and the connected Rule both have now been heard together and are now being disposed of by this judgment. At the time of hearing, a supplementary affidavit has been filed on behalf of the defendant-appellant showing some subsequent developments as stated below in the matter of lease and possession of the fishery in question. 

 6. The plaintiff-respondent being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of safty granted by this Court, moved the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court by a Civil Misc. Petition No. 89 of 1991 and also prayed for an ad-interim order vacating the stay but their Lordships of the Appellate Division by an order dated 28.10.91 refused the prayer for vacating the order of stay of' this Court. It appears that the plaintiff respondent here which was appellant petitioner gradually lost its interest and on the prayer by the learned Advocate the Civil Leave petition was dismissed for non-prosecution by the Appellate Division on 18.10.1991. Thus there was no order of stay dated 21.8.91 earlier granted by a Division Bench of this Court and during this time the appellant received the remaining 50% of the bid money from the new lessee Samity and put the new lessee i.e. Maijchar Doanandi Matsajibi Samabaya Samity into possession of the suit fishery and the necessary lease deed was accordingly made on 2.9.91 and since then the new lessee being recognised as such for 3 years i.e. 1398-1400. B.S are in possession of the fishery. 

 7. Now, Mr. Sajjad Ali Chowdhury, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the defendant-appellant has contended that the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is wholly illegal and unreasonable and the same should be set aside. He has further contended that the learned Subordinate Judge mis-conceived the provisions of law and the principles governing granting of temporary injunction. The learned A.A.G. has taken us through the impugned judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge and also the application for temporary" injunction of the plaintiff and the written objection filed by the defendants. He has pointed out that the learned Subordinate Judge has wrongly found that in view of Rule 205(3) of the Government -Estate Manual, the plaintiff is entitled to get compensatory extension of the lease Such was valid only upto the 30th Chaitra 1397 B.S. He has relied on a decision given in C.P.S.L.A. No. 125 of 1980 in the case of Mohiuddin Ahmed Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others in a nutshel reported in Bangladesh Supreme Court Digest (1980-81) at page 72 and has contended that the rules of the Government Estate Manual are only departmental guidelines which are required to be normally followed in the matter of making any settlement or lease of land or fishery. The guidelines provided in the Estate Manual have got no statutory force and hence the plaintiff Samity cannot claim as a matter of right any compensatory extension of its already expired least. No one appeared for the respondent to oppose the above contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants, but still then we have tried to examine the above contention for the appellant of the question of applicability of the said Estate Manual Rules. It appears to us that the above point relates to the subject matter of the suit involving merit of the same and in all interlocutory application for temporary injunction arising out of the suit, we should not go to make any conclusive observation on the question of the nature and applicability of the said Rules. The decision as cited by the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the appellants of course apparently appears to be in their favour. On a plain reading of the impugned judgment and order 61 the learned judgment Judge, it appears that admittedly the plaintiff was granted lease upto Chaitra 1397 B.S. and it was the case of the plaintiff that it was illegally debarred from taking part in any taking auction of the Government fisheries by an alleged decision dated 23.7.90 of the local Management Committee and that decision has been challenged in the present suit and further the plaintiff was admittedly in the possession of the suit-fishery at the time of institution of the suit. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record found a prima-facie case for the plaintiff. And prima-facie case means where an important question of law and facts required to be decided as per decision reported in 22 DLR (SC) 98. Hence, we do not think that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed any illegality is finding a prima-facie case in favour or the plaintiff-respondent. Now, it is submitted by the learned A.A.G. for the appellant that only on a finding of a prima-facie case alone temporary injunction cannot be granted. In the instant case in fact there is no clear finding as to the other legal requirements for granting temporary injunction i.e. balance of convenience and irreparable loss. It is well known that in the case of granting temporary injunction, the plaintiff must firstly show that he has a prima-facie case, secondly, that he will suffer irreparable loss, if injunction is not granted and thirdly he must show that the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in his favour. The above principles have been well settled in many a decision of our Court and we cite here a few, namely, one in the case of Mia Muhammad Latif Versus Province of West Pakistan reported in 22 D.L.R. (SC) 98 and another in the case of Mst. Aymon Nessa and others Vs. Md. Obaidul Haque and others reported in 35 D.L.R. at page 25. The learned Assistant Attorney-General for the appellant has further pointed out from the impugned judgment that there is not a single word in it on the question of irreparable loss, if any, that the plaintiff may suffer, if injunction is not granted and as regards the question of balance of convenience and in convenience, there is of course a vague finding without any discussion of the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record. It has been further contended by the learned Assistant Attorney-General that if temporary injunction is not granted, the plaintiff shall not suffer any irreparable loss or injury in the instant case because the period of lease of the plaintiff has already expired on 30th Chaitra, 1397 B.S. and the suit fishery has already been leased out to some other fishermen Samabaya Society as stated above and if that society i.e. the new lessees cannot exercise and enjoy their right of lease that will create unnecessary problems for the defendant-appellants and lead to further litigations in the matter and Govt. will be in more disadvantageous position, particularly when the rest of the formalities in respect of the lease to the new lessee for the years 1398-14.00 B.S. have, been completed. Hence, the vague and so-called finding of the trial Court without, any basis is, wholly bad and illegal. Thus it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge has granted temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff in fact only on a finding of the prima-facie case which cannot be sustained In law and must be set aside. In this connection we may rely on a decision in the case of Marghub Siddique Vs. Hamid Ahmed Khan and others reported in 1974 Supreme Court. Monthly Review at page 519, wherein it has been held by their lordships. 

 Injunction is not to be granted only on the basis of existence of prima facie case. It is incumbent of Court to, take into account other questions. 

 8. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent on the day fixed for judgment however submitted that, it has intact, lost its interest to Contest the appeal, as the impugned order of injunction passed by the learned Subordinate Judge has become infructuous for the reason that according to his information the auction of the suit fishery has already been completed and trip new lessee Samity has been nut into Possession of the same and to that effect there is a supplementary affidavit also filed by the defendants appellants and that being the position he does not find any reason to contest the First Misc. Appeal. 

 9. Having regard to our above, discussion and the findings and in view of the submission the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent, we are of the view that the appeal must succeed and the impugned order must be set aside.
